name: Low-latency book: direct-indexed std::array maps for order books
listed_description: Order book keyed by ticker, order id and price using fixed-size std::array tables indexed directly, acting as hash maps with no hashing or node allocation.
book_benchmark: No timing in this chunk; design is reused from the matching engine chapter and only described. Any numbers would be in the performance chapters outside this chunk.
found_in: book: Building Low Latency Applications with C++ (2023), ch. 8, Defining the structures for the market order book; ch. 7, Defining the data members in the snapshot synthesizer

name: Low-latency book: MemPool preallocated object pool
listed_description: Template memory pool, one per object type, preallocated at startup and used for orders, price levels and market updates so the hot path avoids dynamic allocation.
book_benchmark: No timing in this chunk; pool use is only described for order book and snapshot synthesizer. Benchmark, if any, is in an earlier chapter outside this chunk.
found_in: book: Building Low Latency Applications with C++ (2023), ch. 8, Defining the data members in the order book; ch. 7, Initializing the snapshot synthesizer

name: Low-latency book: LFQueue lock-free queue between threads
listed_description: Lock-free queue used to pass market updates, order requests and responses between components running on separate threads.
book_benchmark: No timing in this chunk; queue only used by market data publisher, snapshot synthesizer, order gateway and trade engine.
found_in: book: Building Low Latency Applications with C++ (2023), ch. 7, Defining the data members in the market data publisher; ch. 8, Connecting to the exchange and sending and receiving order flow

name: Low-latency book: price-level linked list order book
listed_description: Limit order book as doubly linked lists of price levels, each holding FIFO lists of orders, with pooled nodes and array lookup by order id and price.
book_benchmark: No timing in this chunk; client order book copies the matching engine design. Design rationale lives in earlier chapter outside this chunk.
guessed_baseline: std::map of price to order list
found_in: book: Building Low Latency Applications with C++ (2023), ch. 8, Building order books from market data
